title: Even the Socinians grant that God pleads with the hardened, as with Pharaoh
source_text: XXI. Caeterum non dedecere sapientiam divinam, ut illos quos Deus certo scit monitis, hortatibus, & praeceptis ipsius nequaquam obtemperaturos, nihilominus compellat, hortetur & invitet modis omnibus ad resipiscentiam, convinci possunt illi ipsi quibus cum nobis res est. Fatentur enim quosdam, divino judicio pertinacem eorum malitiam ulciscente, sic excaecatos & induratos esse, ut resipiscere nequeant. Et tamen negare non possunt Deum erga illos ipsos quos optime novit sic affectos & dispositos esse, uti monitionibus, & obtestationibus quibus homines solet ad officium compellere, ut vel ex solo Pharaonis exemplo manifestum est. Si ergo in his, aut circa hos, fatentibus adversariis, locum habere possunt seriae Dei obtestationes, comminationes, querelae, sine ulla justitiae Dei violatione, aut sapientiae imminutione, cur idem in caeteris, quos Deus ab aeterno, ex libero voluntatis & mentis proposito, novit non obsequuturos, locum habere non valeat?
pass_a_gloss: But that it does not misbecome the divine wisdom, that those whom God certainly knows will by no means obey his admonitions, exhortations, and precepts, he nevertheless urges, exhorts and invites by all means to repentance, those very persons with whom we have to do can be convinced. For they confess that some, the divine judgment avenging their obstinate malice, are so blinded and hardened, that they cannot repent. And yet they cannot deny that God towards those very persons whom he very well knows to be so affected and disposed, uses the admonitions, and adjurations by which he is wont to urge men to duty, as is manifest even from the single example of Pharaoh. If therefore in these, or about these, our adversaries confessing it, serious adjurations, threatenings, complaints of God can have place, without any violation of the justice of God, or diminution of his wisdom, why should not the same be able to have place in the rest, whom God from eternity, from the free purpose of their will and mind, knew would not obey?
pass_b_english: Our opponents themselves can be convinced that it is not unworthy of God's wisdom to urge, exhort and invite to repentance, by every means, those he knows for certain will never obey his warnings, exhortations and commands. They admit that some, by God's judgment punishing their stubborn wickedness, are so blinded and hardened that they cannot repent.

Yet they cannot deny that toward those very people, whom he knows perfectly well to be in that state, God uses the warnings and pleas by which he ordinarily calls human beings to their duty, as the example of Pharaoh alone makes plain.

If, then, by our opponents' own admission, God's earnest pleas, threats and complaints can have a place with such people, without any breach of his justice or loss to his wisdom, why can the same not hold for all the others whom God knew from eternity would not obey, out of the free purpose of their own will and mind?

lemmas.latin: divino judicio pertinacem eorum malitiam ulciscente

from the free purpose of their will and mind

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
